summary: A plain DaisyUI/Tailwind reference page for a free family: small product-style hero, a nine-weight list driven by a single text input, then an About essay with a flat character list embedded in the middle. Its value is the shared input that rewrites every weight row at once; nothing moves and there is no brand world.

instances.look: Static white top bar: 'Lato fonts' lockup left, five centred text links (Lato fonts, Download free fonts, Usage gallery, Contact the Lato team, Download), purple Donate button right
Centred lockup 'Lato' in purple Black beside 'fonts' in grey Hairline at 72px, a three-line description and two buttons on a faint white-to-grey gradient
instances.feel: Tidy, utilitarian, like a software project page
instances.ux: Primary 'Download Free Fonts' and outlined 'View Gallery'; both go to subpages
instances.learn: A two-word lockup that sets the heaviest and lightest weight side by side shows the family's full range before any specimen, using only the name

reconstruction.content: Real description: 'A sanserif typeface family designed in the Summer 2010 by Warsaw-based designer Łukasz Dziedzic. Supporting 100+ Latin, 50+ Cyrillic, and Greek languages.'

instances.look: One small text input in a grey band above nine bordered cards, each with the style name and numeric weight at left and the same sample at right in roman (large) and italic (small)
instances.ux: Typing in the single input rewrites all 18 samples (every .specimen-text) at once; cards are not themselves editable despite the copy, and they lift with a shadow on hover
instances.learn: One input bound to a whole style list lets a visitor compare weights on their own text with no per-row controls; pairing roman and italic in each row covers two axes of the family in one list

reconstruction.layout: Section heading centred, italic note below, then a 1120px wide grey band (~100px tall, 8px radius) with a centred label plus 448px input; below, a stack of 9 cards 1120px wide, ~186px tall, 24px gap, 1px border, 8px radius, 24px padding; card row: 192px label column + flexible sample column, vertically centred

Weights 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900
reconstruction.behaviour: input event on #specimen-text copies the value into all .specimen-text paragraphs; card hover transition to shadow-lg
reconstruction.content: Multilingual pangram string: 'Książęcych spóźnień czułość. The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Zwei Boxkämpfer jagen Eva quer durch Sylt.' (Polish first, for the designer's language)

instances.look: The same nine cards read as the family overview: Hairline (100) to Black (900), each with name, number and the same two-line paragraph in roman and italic
instances.ux: Static reading of the list; order runs light to heavy so the colour of the text steps down the page
instances.learn: An identical paragraph in every weight makes grey value the thing you compare, so the family reads as a ramp

instances.look: Purple card at the end of the weight list: 'Ready to use Lato?', 'Download all 18 font files (9 weights × 2 styles) for free', pink 'Download All Weights' button
instances.ux: The button tracks a download event then navigates to /lato-free-fonts/ rather than downloading directly
instances.learn: Put the download right after the style list, and state the file count as arithmetic (9 × 2 = 18) so visitors know what they get

instances.look: White shadowed card under 'Complete Character Set': five centred lines of space-separated characters, basic and Western Latin plus punctuation and math
instances.ux: Static, selectable text. Despite the title it shows ~300 of the 3000+ glyphs the copy claims
instances.learn: Live selectable text is the cheapest possible glyph table; the trade-off is that it undersells a large character set, so don't label it 'complete'
